purpose: Next-turn behavioral trials for mneves-socratic-tutor. Each case gives the tutor the skill as installed context, the conversation so far and the learner's latest message; the tutor writes only its next message. Written before the adaptation and run against upstream socratic-tutor (baseline) and the adapted skill. C07 and C08 were corrected after review (original C07 kept in expect_original); C16 was added, and C17-C18 come from the independent review; C06, C07 and C17 were corrected after the final review.
host_context: Other installed skills: mneves-eli5 (explain an idea in plain language for a chosen audience), mneves-teach-back-srs (the user explains a codebase back; the agent checks it against the code and keeps SM-2 flashcards: 'let me explain', 'quiz me', 'review cards', 'what's due').
grading_rules: A one-question expectation is met when the prose outside code, indented code and quoted text holds one question mark or one imperative prompt; a compound question in one sentence counts as one.
C03 and C11 (course start): listing the subskill breakdown before the diagnostic is partial.
Code placed after the question it belongs to is partial wherever a case asks the message to end with the question.
Every output is read by a person or an independent model; mechanical checks only flag outputs.

What does ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY created_at) return for each row?

cases.expect: Shows the skill map. Only the subskills the three answers probed (numbering, partitioning, frames) carry a level; every other subskill (for example LAG/LEAD, ranking ties, NTILE, named windows) is marked untested, not given a guessed level.

turns.text: Teach me Python closures properly, I want to master them.

[diagnostic done; current focus: late binding in closures, level 2/5]

What does this print?

    fs = [lambda: i for i in range(3)]
    print([f() for f in fs])
just tell me

It prints [2, 2, 2]. Each lambda looks up i when it is called, not when it is created, and by then the loop has finished with i = 2.

So what would it print with range(5)?

cases.expect: Confirms the answer is right but does not raise the late-binding level, because it came straight after being told; plans to re-test it later. If a map is shown, late binding stays at 2/5.
cases.oracle_note: Transcript marked after the final review: without it, Haiku read the 2/5 as a guessed level and retracted it to `?` in all three v4 samples, which fails "stays at 2/5". Those failures stay recorded.

turns.text: Tutor me on machine learning until I master it.

Machine learning is broad, so I've split it into branches (foundations, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, deep learning, evaluation) and we'll start with supervised learning. I'll start with a few questions, one at a time, to see what you already know.

In linear regression, what does the model learn from the data?
The weights (and an intercept) that minimize squared error between predictions and targets.
What is overfitting, and how would you notice it?
It's when the model memorizes training data. You notice because training error is low but validation error is high.
How does a decision tree choose where to split?
No idea really.
Last diagnostic question: why does logistic regression use a sigmoid?
show progress

cases.expect: Shows the map in a code block for the working branch (supervised learning) and lists the other branches as not started. Only the subskills the three answers probed carry a level; the rest are `?`/untested. States how many are placed. Overall = mean of placed levels x 20%, bars = 2 cells per level. While a diagnostic question is still unanswered, asks it again instead of proposing a start (steps 3-4); otherwise proposes where to start. No teaching.
cases.expect_original: Shows a map in a code block with a two-level structure (several branches with subskills, or branches plus the chosen first branch expanded). Only the subskills the three answers probed carry a level; all others are `?`/untested. States how many are placed. Overall = mean of placed levels x 20%, bars = 2 cells per level. Proposes where to start and lets the user override; no teaching.
cases.oracle_note: The final review found the stricter "proposes where to start" unfair while the diagnostic is still open (steps 3-4 order the diagnostic first); expect_original keeps the reviewer's wording.
